records.subject: Concern over operational and maintenance challenges faced by the UNESCO heritage, Darjeeling Himalayan Railway.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Harsh Vardhan Shringla:

I seek to draw attention to the need to preserve the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, popularly known as the Toy Train, a UNESCO World Heritage Site under the Mountain Railways of India. Built in 1881, this engineering marvel connects New Jalpaiguri to Darjeeling across fragile Himalayan terrain. For over 140 years, it has symbolized the region?s cultural identity and attracted tourists from India and abroad. However, serious operational and maintenance challenges now threaten its survival. Despite efforts by the Ministry of Railways, the railway corridor has gradually shrunk, compromising safety and efficiency. The line passes through landslide-prone areas where heavy rainfall frequently damages tracks and disrupts services, requiring constant monitoring and restoration. Ageing steam locomotives also demand specialised maintenance and custom-built parts, necessitating sustained technical and financial support. The vision of ?Vikaas bhi Viraasat bhi? rightly emphasizes balancing development with heritage conservation. This railway embodies that vision must be preserved through sustainable tourism and infrastructure strengthening. There is a need to enhance visibility through strategic marketing and to develop an integrated tourism ecosystem linked with local culture and livelihoods. Active participation of local communities, tourism stakeholders, and Self Help Groups can generate employment. Skill development of youth and railway staff in heritage conservation and modern maintenance is equally essential.???????? I urge the Government to formulate a comprehensive conservation plan with adequate funding, infrastructure restoration, corridor protection, and disaster mitigation measures. Preserving this railway is preserving a living heritage and the identity of the hills.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for targeted promotion of sports in the Darjeeling hills and the North Bengal region.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Harsh Vardhan Shringla: I rise to request focused promotion of sports in the Darjeeling hills and the North Bengal region. This area has a remarkable football tradition that spans more than a century. Darjeeling was among the earliest centres where the sport took deep root and its schools and local institutions produced players who later joined leading Kolkata clubs. Footballers from the hills have represented Bengal in the Santosh Trophy and served in forces teams that achieved national honours. However, the region today suffers from inadequate sports infrastructure. The absence of quality stadiums and training facilities has pushed this legacy to the margins and local youths from the place are unable to place them in state, regional and national teams. North Bengal also has immense potential in adventure and outdoor sports. Its terrain is ideal for trekking, rock climbing, paragliding, mountain biking and river activities. Darjeeling already has a heritage of mountaineering training through institutions like the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute. What is needed now is upgraded infrastructure, new adventure circuits, certified safety systems and coordinated promotion to attract both domestic and international participants. Under the leadership of the Hon?ble Prime Minister, the Government has prioritised sports excellence and youth development through initiatives like Khelo India. In this context, Darjeeling hills deserve a dedicated football academy, high quality turf grounds and a regional plan covering football, hockey, indoor and adventure sports. I therefore request for three integrated sports centres in Darjeeling, Kalimpong and Kurseong, and one training centre in Mirik.

(ENDS)
